harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired `/srv/legacy2/stale-pidfile-startup/bin/control` on node1. It now distinguishes live, stale, foreign, and missing PID states; safely recovers stale PID files; keeps repeated starts at one worker; and never signals unrelated processes. The original journal content was preserved and continues growing. Node1 rebooted successfully and recovered with the installed OS/kernel unchanged. Final state: one worker running, SSH active, and SELinux enforcing.
actions_performed: Diagnosed the file-existence-only PID handling and reproduced the stale-PID startup failure.
Replaced only `bin/control`, preserving root:root ownership and mode 0755.
Added exact worker identity checks and serialized control actions using the installed util-linux `flock`.
Tested stale PID recovery, foreign PID safety, idempotent starts, worker stopping, and journal preservation.
Rebooted node1 exactly once and verified its changed boot identity and post-restart recovery.
Removed temporary test processes and files; left one intended worker running.

evidence.summary: The original controller trusted PID-file existence; PID 99999999 was nonexistent, status incorrectly returned success, and start returned RC 1.
Used the already-installed util-linux 2.40.2 `flock`; the repaired POSIX shell script passed syntax validation and retained root:root ownership and mode 0755.
Stale PID status returned RC 1; start removed it and launched a worker; live status returned RC 0.

evidence.requirement: Repeated starts retain exactly one worker
evidence.summary: Repeated starts returned success with an unchanged PID and exact worker count of one; final PID is 891.

evidence.requirement: Distinguish foreign PIDs and preserve unrelated processes
evidence.summary: Foreign status returned RC 3. Both foreign-PID stop and worker start/stop paths left the unrelated process alive; the temporary process was subsequently cleaned up.
The SHA-256 of the original 37-byte journal prefix remained `1c52071e...29c1ab4` before and after testing/reboot, while normal worker ticks appended to the file.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID and worker/data state; reboot acknowledgement returned RC 0; boot ID changed from `2b19e976-dee2-4700-9045-90d61b6dcffe` to `cfc61fc4-163b-42ae-969e-43322c678373`; repaired control recovered the reboot-stale PID and restored one healthy worker.

evidence.requirement: Preserve OS, kernel, security, and administrative access
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained installed; SSH is active/enabled and listening; SELinux remains enforcing; relevant package versions are unchanged.
